text:

 The Pros:
 Drinks: The drinks were excellent. I had the Guavacita, and the guava and coconut flavor combination was delicious and unique.
 Menu: There is a really solid number of vegetarian options, which is always appreciated.
 

 The Cons:
 The Food: While the drinks and atmosphere are top-tier, the food was a bit letdown for the price point. The chipotle chicken taco was very average. The chicken felt overcooked. We also asked to add cheese to the burrito, but there was hardly any in it.
 

 Honestly, comparing it to a spot like Aqui, you're paying a lot more here for not as great food. That said, Milagros definitely wins on the atmosphere and drink menu. Come for the cocktails and the ambiance, but maybe skip the heavy entrees.

text: I’ve been to Mazra a few times now and it honestly never misses. I ordered the salmon plate and she got the steak shawarma plate. Everything tasted super fresh, flavorful, and like it was actually made with care. The service was great too. text:
I’ve been to both Mazra locations in San Bruno and Redwood City, and I can confidently say the quality and flavor are exactly the same across both locations. Consistently high quality, delicious, fresh, and incredibly flavorful food every single time. The staff are always welcoming, professional, and classy. They truly make you feel appreciated as a customer, and the hospitality stands out just as much as the food.
 

 We had the chicken and fries, which is basically incredibly flavorful rotisserie chicken paired with their house fries. The fries are perfectly crispy, well seasoned, and the portion is very generous. Their toum never disappoints either. It’s tangy, fresh, bold, and absolutely addictive.
 

 Their barbecue meats are excellent across the board, especially the kafta ground beef. The shrimp tasted clean, fresh, and packed with flavor. The cauliflower was incredible as well. The falafel was good too. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. I’ve had better falafel elsewhere, but this was still very enjoyable and well made.
 

 The Arayes were absolutely crisp and packed with flavorful ground meat. The seasoning and texture were excellent, though I do wish there was a bit more meat in the stuffing.
 

 The lamb shank was one of the highlights of the meal. Slow cooked for six hours and unbelievably tender. The sauce from the lamb shank over the rice was absolutely incredible and full of deep flavor. Truly delightful.
 

 And let’s not forget the halloumi cheese rolls. Adding honey takes them to another level. The balance between the salty cheese and the sweetness of the honey is absolutely perfect.
 

 We also took some shawarma wraps and a falafel wrap to go. Not pictured, but absolutely delicious.
 

 For drinks, we tried the melon pineapple refresher, which was refreshing, flavorful, and not overly sweet. We ended the meal with their unique tea, where you can really taste the cardamom, cloves, and other warm spices in the blend. Absolutely incredible experience overall.

My favorite recently was this amazing Agua Chile De Cameron — a perfect mix of shrimps, mango, veggies and nuts, super flavorful but still light and refreshing. Their ceviche mixto is also a must-try, probably one of the best I’ve had, especially with the plantain chips. They always have a non alcoholic drink option which is always a plus, and they even recommended an off-menu rum-based drink (Summer Bikini) that was smooth and perfect for daytime.

text:
I recently visited La Viga Seafood & Cocina Mexicana on Broadway in downtown Redwood City, a well-known spot for Baja-style seafood and coastal Mexican cuisine. The restaurant sits right in the heart of the downtown dining corridor, making it an easy stop if you are exploring the area or coming from nearby Palo Alto or San Mateo.
 

 The atmosphere at La Viga Seafood & Cocina Mexicana feels lively but relaxed. The dining room has a bright, coastal aesthetic that reflects the seafood-focused menu. The space feels casual but polished enough for a proper sit-down meal rather than just a quick taco stop.
 

 To start, we ordered a trio of ceviches presented on a long tasting platter. Each one had a distinct personality. One leaned bright and citrusy with red onion and avocado, another incorporated mango for a slightly sweet balance, and the green aguachile-style preparation had a fresh herbaceous heat. The seafood tasted very fresh and the acidity was well balanced.
 

 We also tried the taco trio which included a crispy fish taco, a battered shrimp taco, and a steak taco topped with salsa and queso fresco. The seafood tacos were the highlight, with light batter and vibrant toppings that kept everything balanced.
 

 Another standout was the fried calamari served with a green dipping sauce and lime. The coating was crisp without being overly heavy.
 

 To finish, we shared churros with chocolate sauce, a classic dessert that ended the meal on a simple but satisfying note.
 

 Having eaten seafood and ceviche across Latin America and coastal markets around the world, La Viga Seafood & Cocina Mexicana does a solid job representing Baja-inspired seafood flavors in the Bay Area.
 

 Overall, La Viga Seafood & Cocina Mexicana delivers fresh seafood, bright flavors, and a comfortable atmosphere that makes it a reliable option when you are craving coastal Mexican cuisine in Redwood City.
label: Positive

text:
Crouching Tiger in Redwood City is a good choice for a big group gathering. They have a ton of spacious tables perfect for family-style dining, and our service was fantastic. The staff was friendly, attentive, and kept our water glasses full throughout the meal.
 

 Unfortunately, the food itself was a bit of a mixed bag. The Vegetarian Manchurian house special had a decent sauce, but the Manchurian itself was a bit soggy on the inside. It felt like it had been sitting in sauce for a bit too long. The egg fried rice with BBQ pork was another letdown. The rice was undercooked, and the BBQ pork itself was bland and lacked the smoky sweetness you would expect.
 

 The hot iron plate style chicken had so much potential, but the execution fell flat. They put the chicken on top of the crispy rice, which sounds good in theory, but it meant the rice got soggy almost immediately. By the time you got to the rice, it was all mushy.
 

 Overall, Crouching Tiger is a good option for a large group with friendly service, but the food needs some work. I'd recommend sticking with simpler dishes and maybe skipping the sizzling plate options.

text:
Probably one of the first customers here since they just opened and there were almost no reviews when I came, so I honestly kept my expectations pretty low.

After dining here, I was surprised by how polished everything already felt. It didn’t feel like a newly opened place still figuring things out.

Sitting at the counter was a great experience — you can watch the chef prepare and serve each course, and the pacing felt smooth and relaxed. No rushing, no trying too hard to create a luxury atmosphere, just a comfortable and focused dining experience.

The omakase itself had a nice flow. From appetizers to sashimi, warm dishes, and finally the nigiri, each course transitioned naturally and didn’t feel repetitive. A few pieces of nigiri really stood out — the fish quality was excellent and the rice was balanced without overpowering the flavor. I especially enjoyed the seared course and some of the tuna selections.

One thing that surprised me: the portion was actually very satisfying. I expected a typical fine dining omakase where you leave wanting more, but this was a full meal and I left genuinely full — not because of extra rice, but because the pacing and portions were thoughtfully done.

Since the restaurant is brand new and doesn’t have many reviews yet, I hope they can keep this level of quality consistently.

Would definitely come back

text:
I finally got to try Mikiya after hearing so many people talk about it and I can definitely see why it’s popular

The concept is fun, the restaurant looks great, and having all-you-can-eat wagyu shabu is something you don’t find everywhere. We went with the middle-tier menu, which honestly felt like the best value unless you’re planning to eat a crazy amount of A5. The quality of the meat was good and the sukiyaki broth was probably my favorite part of the meal.

That said, I walked away feeling like it’s still pretty expensive for what you actually get. By the time you add tax and tip, it’s an easy $100+ per person, and I’m not sure the overall experience justified that price for me.

Service was perfectly fine. Nothing bad happened, but it also wasn’t the kind of hospitality that really stood out. The hosts and servers were polite, food came out quickly, and everything was pretty smooth. Just not especially memorable

One thing I did wonder about was the reviews. I’m not saying anything inappropriate is happening, but with ratings this high, I always hope restaurants are also finding ways to collect honest feedback from regular guests about both the service and overall quality. Sometimes those comments are even more valuable than another five-star rating because they help a good restaurant become an even better one

Overall, it’s a good place if you’re craving AYCE wagyu and want to celebrate something or go with friends. I enjoyed it, but for the price, I personally expected a little more from the overall dining experience. I’d probably come back once in a while, just not as often as I originally thought
